input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 binds us to Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the entire three-year term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no exit on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. That is exclusive dealing for the full term without a performance-based exit — walk-away territory, and it fails the fallback. Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity commitment does not cure the problem: it conflicts with the express grant in Section 2.2 and the order-of-precedence clause (the second Section 2.2) does not resolve an internal conflict within the Agreement. We therefore convert the appointment to non-exclusive, reaching the preferred position and aligning Section 2.2 with Section 12.3. We also note the duplicate "2.2" numbering, which should be renumbered.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any other supplier at any time.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a sole-supplier commitment, so we have made Vendor's appointment non-exclusive; our playbook position is that we retain freedom to source from other suppliers, and this also removes the conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity commitment.
proposal.summary: Make Vendor a non-exclusive provider; remove full-term exclusivity on Customer.
